assets.name: Apple Inc.
assets.summary: Apple Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, and accessories worldwide. The company offers iPhone, a line of smartphones; Mac, a line of personal computers; iPad, a line of multi-purpose tablets; and wearables, home, and accessories comprising AirPods, Apple Vision Pro, Apple TV, Apple Watch, Beats products, and HomePod, as well as Apple branded and third-party accessories. It also provides AppleCare support and cloud services; and operates various platforms, including the App Store that allow customers to discover and download applications and digital content, such as books, music, video, games, and podcasts, as well as advertising services include third-party licensing arrangements and its own advertising platforms. In addition, the company offers various subscription-based services, such as Apple Arcade, a game subscription service; Apple Fitness+, a personalized fitness service; Apple Music, which offers users a curated listening experience with on-demand radio stations; Apple News+, a subscription news and magazine service; Apple TV, which offers exclusive original content and live sports; Apple Card, a co-branded credit card; and Apple Pay, a cashless payment service, as well as licenses its intellectual property. The company serves consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and the education, enterprise, and government markets. It distributes third-party applications for its products through the App Store. The company also sells its products through its retail and online stores, and direct sales force; and third-party cellular network carriers and resellers. The company was formerly known as Apple Computer, Inc. and changed its name to Apple Inc. in January 2007. Apple Inc. was founded in 1976 and is headquartered in Cupertino, California.

latest_news.headline: South Korea's SK Hynix eyes US listing as soon as August, sources say
latest_news.summary: STORY: SK Hynix reportedly plans to list its shares in the U.S. as soon as August.  That's according to two sources familiar with the matter...  The South Korean memory chipmaker wants to capitalise on strong appetite for AI-linked stocks and broaden its investor base.  One source added the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is likely to approve SK Hynix's American listing application during the week of June 22nd.  SK Hynix said in March it had confidentially filed for a U.S. listing.  A source said at the time the offering could raise as much as $14 billion.  The company is the world's second-largest memory chipmaker and a key supplier to Nvidia.  It's scored big in the AI boom due to its dominant position in high-bandwidth memory chips used in AI servers.  Its share price has jumped 240% this year and its market value has topped $1 trillion since May.  That makes it only the third Asian company after Taiwan's TSMC and Samsung Electronics to hit the milestone.  An August debut would also add another top name to what is shaping up to be a busy second half for U.S. equity markets.

Coughlin is direct about the significance: "We very clearly have a standalone mine potential project there for silver and antimony." With high-grade veins at Margaritas and a growing porphyry cluster at Güíntar four kilometres to the north, geological evidence is beginning to suggest the two systems may be connected. latest_news.headline: Crypto Weekly: Saylor's bitcoin sale, Greece mulls crypto tax
latest_news.summary: STORY: From Michael Saylor's bitcoin sale to Greece's potential new tax... This is Crypto Weekly.  :: Crypto Weekly  :: Bitcoin hovers around key $60,000 mark  Bitcoin hovered around the key $60,000 mark.  But that hasn't stopped Standard Chartered's Geoffrey Kendrick feeling bullish about it.  He's the lender's global head of digital assets research.  Kendrick stuck with his call for bitcoin to hit $100,000 by the end of the year as most of the selling may be over.  But he did call it a 'painful' week as the crypto token fell more than 12%.  It also saw one of the highest profile holders of the token made a sale.  Michael Saylor's Strategy said it had shed some of its holdings for the first in four years.  Strategy is the largest corporate holder of bitcoin.  :: Reform UK gets big crypto funding  Reform UK raised more money than any of its political rivals for the third quarter in a row.  That's what data from Britain's Electoral Commission showed.  Nigel Farage's party saw big donations from billionaire crypto investors, including the Thailand-based Christopher Harborne.  Reform raised around $12.4 million in the first three months of the year, while the governing Labour party took in just over $5.3 million.  :: Greece 'prepares' crypto capital gains tax  Greece could be moving towards taxing gains on cryptocurrency.  That's what two government officials told Reuters.  They said lawmakers are preparing legislation to impose a 15% capital gains tax on crypto.  A senior government official told Reuters the Finance Ministry is readying a law that's expected to be submitted to the country's parliament in the coming months.  :: Japan banks plan to issue stablecoins  And Japan's three largest banks said they will jointly issue stablecoins during the current fiscal year ending in March 2027.  It would mark a major move towards digital payments in a country where cash and credit cards are still popular.  Mitsubishi Financial Group, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group and Mizuho Financial Group announced the update.  They said they will set up a council to examine the operational frameworks and prepare for the issuance.

companies.name: Apple Inc.
companies.summary: Apple Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, and accessories worldwide. The company offers iPhone, a line of smartphones; Mac, a line of personal computers; iPad, a line of multi-purpose tablets; and wearables, home, and accessories comprising AirPods, Apple Vision Pro, Apple TV, Apple Watch, Beats products, and HomePod, as well as Apple branded and third-party accessories. It also provides AppleCare support and cloud services; and operates various platforms, including the App Store that allow customers to discover and download applications and digital content, such as books, music, video, games, and podcasts, as well as advertising services include third-party licensing arrangements and its own advertising platforms. In addition, the company offers various subscription-based services, such as Apple Arcade, a game subscription service; Apple Fitness+, a personalized fitness service; Apple Music, which offers users a curated listening experience with on-demand radio stations; Apple News+, a subscription news and magazine service; Apple TV, which offers exclusive original content and live sports; Apple Card, a co-branded credit card; and Apple Pay, a cashless payment service, as well as licenses its intellectual property. The company serves consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and the education, enterprise, and government markets. It distributes third-party applications for its products through the App Store. The company also sells its products through its retail and online stores, and direct sales force; and third-party cellular network carriers and resellers. The company was formerly known as Apple Computer, Inc. and changed its name to Apple Inc. in January 2007. Apple Inc. was founded in 1976 and is headquartered in Cupertino, California.

companies.summary: NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company. The company operates through two segments, Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments. The Compute & Networking segment provides data center accelerated computing and networking platforms and artificial intelligence solutions and software, and automotive platforms and autonomous and electric vehicle solutions, including software. The Graphics segment offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs; Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The company's products are used in gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. The company sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, original device manufacturers, system integrators and distributors, independent software vendors, cloud service providers, add-in board manufacturers, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants worldwide. The company has a strategic collaboration with Tech Mahindra Limited, Lumentum Holdings Inc., Nebius Group N.V., IREN Limited, and SK hynix Inc. NVIDIA Corporation was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

latest_news.headline: South Korea's SK Hynix eyes US listing as soon as August, sources say
latest_news.summary: STORY: SK Hynix reportedly plans to list its shares in the U.S. as soon as August.  That's according to two sources familiar with the matter...  The South Korean memory chipmaker wants to capitalise on strong appetite for AI-linked stocks and broaden its investor base.  One source added the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is likely to approve SK Hynix's American listing application during the week of June 22nd.  SK Hynix said in March it had confidentially filed for a U.S. listing.  A source said at the time the offering could raise as much as $14 billion.  The company is the world's second-largest memory chipmaker and a key supplier to Nvidia.  It's scored big in the AI boom due to its dominant position in high-bandwidth memory chips used in AI servers.  Its share price has jumped 240% this year and its market value has topped $1 trillion since May.  That makes it only the third Asian company after Taiwan's TSMC and Samsung Electronics to hit the milestone.  An August debut would also add another top name to what is shaping up to be a busy second half for U.S. equity markets.
